items.question: Up to what wind speed has starting and stopping the rotor been demonstrated, with the wind from any direction?
options: 30 kt (56 km/h)
40 kt (74 km/h)
50 kt (93 km/h)
items.explanation: Starting and stopping the rotor has been demonstrated for winds of 40 kt (74 km/h) from any direction, and 50 kt (93 km/h) with a headwind (forward center axis ±30°).

items.question: For hover in ground effect (IGE), at sea level, what wind speed from any direction has been demonstrated?
options: Up to 10 kt (19 km/h)
Up to 17 kt (31 km/h)
Up to 23 kt (43 km/h)
Up to 30 kt (56 km/h)
items.explanation: At sea level, controllability for HIGE has been demonstrated for winds up to 30 kt (56 km/h) from any direction, at the maximum weight shown in the HIGE chart.

items.question: Above 7000 ft density altitude, which wind sector has the lowest demonstrated hover wind speed?
options: The most unfavorable sector, at 10 kt (19 km/h)
A tailwind, at 5 kt (9 km/h)
A crosswind, at 15 kt (28 km/h)
There is no reduced sector above 7000 ft
items.explanation: Above 7000 ft (2134 m) density altitude, hover wind has been demonstrated up to 10 kt (19 km/h) in the most unfavorable sector, versus 17 kt (31 km/h) for other azimuths.

items.question: What must the pilot check before takeoff, in HIGE at 5 ft and before initiating forward flight?
options: That the N1 can increase by at least 1% without exceeding the max. transient rating when the collective is pulled slightly
That the TOT margin is positive on the ground
That the VEMD FLI page shows GOOD
That fuel flow is within 5% of the planned value
items.explanation: In HIGE at 5 ft (1.5 m) and before initiating forward flight, the pilot pulls the collective slightly to ensure the N1 can increase by at least 1%, without exceeding the max. transient rating.

items.question: The engine health check on the AS350 B3e verifies which two margins?
options: TRQ MARGIN ISO N1 and TRQ MARGIN ISO TOT
Torque margin and t4 margin
Ng margin and NR margin
Fuel flow margin and oil pressure margin
items.explanation: The engine health check consists of checking TRQ MARGIN ISO N1 and TRQ MARGIN ISO TOT, using either the FADEC (VEMD) procedure or manually recorded parameters.

items.question: Under what conditions must the FADEC engine health check be performed?
options: In level flight at MCP, heating and demisting OFF, stabilized for at least 2 minutes
In a climb at MTOP, heating ON
During autorotation, at any altitude
On the ground at idle, with the rotor brake applied
items.explanation: The engine health check is performed in level flight MCP, heating and demisting system OFF, at an altitude where the engine operates close to the N1 MCP limit, stabilized for at least 2 minutes before the check.

items.question: On the AS350 B3e, the engine health check is satisfactory if:
options: TRQ MARGIN ISO N1 and TRQ MARGIN ISO TOT are both positive (≥0%)
Only TRQ MARGIN ISO TOT needs to be positive
T4 margin is negative and torque margin is positive
Ng is above 100% for at least 1 minute
items.explanation: The engine health check is satisfactory if both TRQ MARGIN ISO N1 and TRQ MARGIN ISO TOT are positive (≥0%, "GOOD" displayed).

items.question: Before recording parameters for the manual engine health check procedure, to what value must the altimeter be set?
options: QNH
Field elevation QFE
1000 hPa
items.explanation: The altimeter must be set to 1013.2 hPa to display Hp before recording the parameters used in the manual engine health check.

items.question: In the height-velocity (HV) diagram, how is point A of the avoidance zone defined?
options: 100 ft height, variable airspeed
25 ft height, 40 kt constant airspeed
8 ft skid height at zero airspeed
Variable height at zero airspeed
items.explanation: Point A is the low hover point: 8 ft (2.5 m) skid height at zero airspeed.

items.question: What glide performance is published for autorotation?
options: 0.54 NM per 1000 ft at IAS = 65 kt and NR ≥ 410 rpm
1.0 NM per 1000 ft at IAS = 80 kt and NR ≥ 386 rpm
0.25 NM per 1000 ft at IAS = 50 kt and NR ≥ 400 rpm
0.75 NM per 1000 ft at IAS = 65 kt and NR ≥ 420 rpm
items.explanation: The distance flown in autorotation is 0.54 NM per 1000 ft at an IAS of 65 kt and NR ≥ 410 rpm (1000 m per 300 m height at 120 km/h).
